clue.text: Applauding picking for international match outside left

indicators.note: the selection word wraps around the abbreviation for left, so it stands outside it

parts.note: a player picked for his country is awarded a cap, so selecting is capping

explanation.surface: A sports fan cheers as a player is picked for an international side to play on the left wing.
explanation.definitionFit: Clapping is the act of striking the hands together in approval, the usual form of applause.

clue.text: Cold chop to munch

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
to hew is to chop with an axe

explanation.surface: A cold pork chop for eating.
explanation.definitionFit: To chew is to bite and grind food with the teeth, which is what munching involves.

clue.text: Ninety degrees, say, needed for fish

definitions.meaning: a right ... is ninety degrees, an example of an ...
to fish with rod and line

explanation.surface: An angler insists the rod must be held at a right angle to catch anything.
explanation.definitionFit: Angle is both a geometric measure between lines and the verb for fishing with a hook.

clue.text: Just like Washington, say, putting parking above providing places to live?

indicators.note: in a down answer the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for parking on road signs
residential describes an area of homes

explanation.surface: A planner wonders whether putting a car park over housing is very Washington.
explanation.walkthrough: Washington could be the city; it is George Washington, the first US president.
explanation.definitionFit: Presidential means befitting a president, and George Washington was the first one.

clue.text: Deny in former London prison losing weight

indicators.note: the prison's name drops a letter, so it is removed

parts.note: Newgate was a notorious London jail, demolished in 1904

explanation.surface: An inmate of an old London jail denies wasting away.
explanation.walkthrough: NEWGATE was a famous London prison, closed in 1902.
explanation.definitionFit: To negate is to deny the truth or existence of something, to nullify it.

clue.text: Note picture is a very long film, perhaps

parts.note: E is one of the musical notes A to G
pic is a short informal word for a picture or photo; that the letters also run across the printed words is a coincidence, with no indicator for it

explanation.surface: A remark that some motion picture runs for a very long time.
explanation.definitionFit: An epic is a grand, lengthy cinematic production; 'perhaps' signals that a long film is only one example.

clue.text: Bearing costs centrally, cutting 100%

indicators.note: the central letters slice into the word for total, sitting inside it

parts.note: something 100% is pure

indicators.note: only the central letters of the word are used

explanation.surface: A business bears the costs at head office by slashing them entirely.
explanation.definitionFit: Bearing can mean the way a person carries themselves, which is posture.

clue.text: Old video format prescribed in class

indicators.note: the word for prescribed is placed inside the word for class

parts.note: a caste is a social class
set means fixed or prescribed, as a set text

explanation.surface: A teacher shows the class a recommended film on an outdated tape.
explanation.definitionFit: Video cassettes such as VHS tapes were the standard home recording medium before discs.

clue.text: Some unusual matter in strangely inapt newspaper feature

indicators.note: the word is rearranged in an odd way

parts.note: an article is a piece in a newspaper

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece about odd stuff is oddly unsuitable.
explanation.definitionFit: Antimatter is made of antiparticles, so one is a piece of that unusual form of matter.

clue.text: Large bird eaten by hunting hounds?

indicators.note: the bird is swallowed whole by the hounds' name, so only the inside of that word is kept

parts.note: beagles are small dogs bred for hunting hares

explanation.surface: A whimsical picture of a big bird of prey ending up as dinner for a pack of hunting dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside BEAGLES: 'eaten by' strips the outer B and S. The question mark admits the device is playful.
explanation.definitionFit: The eagle is one of the biggest raptors, a powerful bird of prey with a huge wingspan.

clue.text: Information is needed about European society's origin

indicators.note: the information and the word is go about, that is either side of, the pair of abbreviations

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
S abbreviates society

explanation.surface: Someone researching the founding of a European society says more facts are required.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' places GEN and IS either side of E and S. GEN is British slang for information or facts.
explanation.definitionFit: Genesis is the beginning or birth of something, as in the first book of the Bible recounting creation.

clue.text: Again circulate glowing eulogy about one son

indicators.note: the colour and the praise go around, either side of, the numeral and the abbreviation

parts.note: something glowing hot is red
a eulogy is a tribute of praise
I is the Roman numeral one
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A proud parent shares an admiring speech about their boy with everyone again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' places RED and TRIBUTE either side of I and S.
explanation.definitionFit: To redistribute is to hand something out once more, spreading it round anew among recipients.

clue.text: Constant inclination for housework?

parts.note: C is the symbol for a constant in mathematics and physics
a leaning is an inclination or tendency

explanation.surface: Someone who has a permanent urge to do the chores.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleaning is a typical domestic chore; the question mark marks it as an example of housework.

clue.text: Poodle, perhaps with some black eye

indicators.note: only part of the following words is taken, so the answer lies within them

explanation.surface: Describes a dog, maybe a poodle, sporting a dark patch around one eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poodle' looks like the dog; in British usage a poodle is a servile follower, as when a prime minister was called the president's poodle.
explanation.definitionFit: A lackey is a fawning servant who does another's bidding, which is what a political 'poodle' is.

clue.text: Ship curries all over the place

indicators.note: scattered in disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A vessel spilling curries everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: A cruiser is a warship or a large pleasure boat.

clue.text: A million involved in fast must be keen

indicators.note: the letter and abbreviation are wrapped up inside the period of fasting

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting before Easter

explanation.surface: Suggests anyone joining a fast of a million people has to be enthusiastic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keen' looks like an adjective meaning eager; here it is the verb to wail in grief.
explanation.definitionFit: To keen is to wail in mourning, so it is a synonym of lament as a verb.

clue.text: Grating last of cheese to go under cooker

indicators.note: in a down answer this piece sits below the cooker word

parts.note: a grill is a cooker or part of one

indicators.note: the final letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A kitchen instruction to grate the remaining cheese and put it beneath the grill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grating' looks like a verb about cheese; it is the noun for a grid of bars.
explanation.definitionFit: A grille is a framework of bars, a grating over a window or opening.

clue.text: Grown-up with ecstasy to share out, mixing with inferior stuff

parts.note: an adult is a grown-up
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
to ration is to share out in limited amounts

explanation.surface: An adult with ecstasy tablets to hand around is cutting them with cheap filler.
explanation.definitionFit: Adulteration is the debasing of a substance by blending in cheaper or impure ingredients.

clue.text: Housekeeper and wife in unit on top of restaurant

indicators.note: the abbreviation is placed inside the word for unit

parts.note: one is a single unit

indicators.note: in a down answer the top is the first letter

explanation.surface: A cleaner and his wife live in a flat above a restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: Housekeeper suggests a cleaner; cryptically it is one who keeps (possesses) a house.
explanation.definitionFit: Read literally, a house-keeper is someone who holds a house, which an owner does.

clue.text: Feign endless embarrassment for one's actions

indicators.note: the word loses its last letter

parts.note: shame is the embarrassment felt for what one has done

explanation.surface: Someone pretends to feel unending embarrassment over what they did.
explanation.definitionFit: To sham is to pretend or fake something, the same as to feign it.

clue.text: Poles dividing it all to invest in office

indicators.note: the two letters split the phrase apart by sitting inside it

parts.note: the two words taken together as written
N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: Polish people splitting everything up before putting money into an office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' looks like the nationality but gives N and S, the two compass poles.
explanation.definitionFit: To install someone is formally to place them in a post, as a new bishop or official is installed.

clue.text: Mollusc caught once mostly by the end of beach

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: most of the word is kept, its final letter dropped
the final letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: A shellfish was picked up once on a stretch of shore.
explanation.definitionFit: A conch is a large sea snail, a mollusc with a spiral shell.

clue.text: Leave, concerned with spilt blood

parts.note: to go is to leave
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone departs because they are worried about a bloody spill.
explanation.definitionFit: Gore is blood shed from a wound, especially when clotted, as in a violent scene.

clue.text: Message Marjorie allowed to be returned

indicators.note: sent back, so the name and the word for allowed are read from the end

parts.note: Marge is a short form of Marjorie
let means allowed

explanation.surface: A note sent to Marjorie is permitted to be sent back.
explanation.definitionFit: A telegram is a message sent by telegraph and delivered in printed form.
